1.4: 1.4 Noah. Rabanus on Paralipomenon, vol. 3. Noah is shown as the tenth from Adam both in Genesis and in Paralipomenon, and aptly the tenth, because he is perfect. Hence, Noah was a just and perfect man in his generations, etc. (Gen. 6). He begot Shem, Ham and Japheth, through whom after the flood the revived offspring of men is spread abroad.
1.5: 1.5 The sons of Japheth. Jerome. These possessed the land in Asia, from Amanus and Taurus, the mountains of Syria, Cheles and Cilicia, to the river Tanais. In Europe, as far as Gades, leaving names to places and peoples, of which many were afterward changed, the rest remain. Tubal. Rabanus. The Iberians, who are also Spaniards, from whom Celtiberia, although some suspect the Italians. Meshech. The same. The Cappadocians, whence their city is to this day called Masaca. But the Septuagint translators think Gapthorim are the Cappadocians.
1.7: 1.7 And the sons. Gregory. From these were divided the islands of the nations, the tongues, kinships and peoples. From the Ionians, that is the Greeks, are born the Elisaeans, who are also the Aeolians. Hence this language is called in Greek Aeolic. Tarshish. Rabanus. Josephus thinks these are the Cilicians, whence their capital is also called Tarsus, glorious for the apostle Paul (Acts 22). Kittim. The same. From whom the Cithaeans, otherwise the Cithians, from whom the city of Cyprus, Cithia, otherwise Cithium, is called to this day. Dodanim. The same. The Rhodians, for so the Septuagint translated. Let us read the books of Varro on antiquities and of Sinnius Capito, and the Greek Phlegon and the rest, and we shall see that almost all the islands and the shores of the whole world, and the seacoast lands, were occupied by Greek settlers: who from Amanus and Taurus possessed all the maritime parts as far as the British ocean.
1.8: 1.8 Put. The same. The Libyans, from whom also a river of Mauritania is called Put, and the region Putensis. Many writers, Greek as well as Latin, are witnesses of this. But why in one part of the climate the ancient name of Libya remains, and the rest of the land is called Africa, is not for this time to discuss.
1.9: 1.9 Seba. The same. From whom the Sabaeans; Saba is now interpreted as Arabia, hence in Psalm 71 where we have: The kings of the Arabians and Saba; in the Hebrew it has: The kings of Saba and Saba, the first with Shin, the second with Samech.
1.10: 1.10 He began to be mighty on the earth. Because he first seized an unaccustomed tyranny. He was a mighty hunter before the Lord, because he turned men away from the worship of God. Hence Josephus: He made them puffed up to the injury and contempt of God. Nimrod, son of Cush, son of Ham, son of Noah, who, being more daring and very strong of hand, persuaded men not to ascribe their happiness to God, but to their own virtue. So he called men back from the fear of God, that they might place hope in their own strength. And therefore they thought God was threatening a flood. Hence they urged that a tower be built which the water could not climb. And the multitude was ready to obey Nimrod, thinking it a grievous servitude to comply with God. Nimrod reigned in Babylon and in Erech. This is Edessa, and Accad, which is Nisibis, and in Calneh, which was called Seleucia from King Seleucus, or which is now called Ctesiphon.
1.11: 1.11 And Mizraim begot. Rabanus. Except the Lehabim, from whom the Libyans are named, who were formerly Putaeans, and the Casluhim, who afterward were called Philistines, whom we corruptly call Palestinians. The other peoples are unknown to us, because, overthrown in the Ethiopian war, they passed into oblivion of their former names. They possessed the land from Gaza to the farthest borders of Egypt.
1.14: 1.14 The Girgashite, the Hivite. He founded the town of Arca opposite Tripolis at the foot of Lebanon, not far from which was another city named Sim, which, overthrown by the varying fortunes of wars, kept only its former name for the place.
1.16: 1.16 The Arvadite also. From whom the Arvadites, who possessed the island of Arvad, separated by a narrow strait from the Phoenician shore. And the Zemarite. From whom the city of Samaria of Coele-Syria, now also so called by Syrians and Hebrews as formerly among the ancients. The Hamathite. Rabanus. From whom the city Hamath. The Macedonians who reigned in the East after Alexander named it Epiphania. Others think it was called Antioch. Others, consulting their opinion with a not truly plausible term, think that Emmaus, the first stage from Antioch for those going to Edessa, is called so, and the same among the ancients Hamath.
1.17: 1.17 The sons of Shem, etc. These hold the parts of Asia from the Euphrates to the Indian ocean. There is Elam, from whom the princes of Persia. Uz and Hul. Or Us, founder of Trachonitis and Damascus, held the principate between Palestine and Coele-Syria, from whom the land of Uz of which Job was; hence, according to the Septuagint, there was a man in the region of Ausitis named Job, as it were of Uz.
1.19: 1.19 Peleg. Rabanus. By a certain prophecy. For Peleg means division, because in his days the tongues were divided in Babylon. Philo tells in the book of Questions on Genesis that from the three sons of Noah, while he was still living, were born thirteen thousand one hundred men, apart from women and little ones, having leaders over themselves. The sons of Shem, Joktan as leader; the sons of Ham, Nimrod; the sons of Japheth, Suphene. After the death of Noah the leaders came with their armies into the plain of Shinar to build a tower there. As they were building, God divided their tongues, and changed their appearances, and each did not recognize his brother, nor hear the tongue of his neighbor. When the masters sought stones, the servants brought water, and when they asked for water, they brought straw. And so, their plan frustrated, they ceased to build and were scattered over the face of the earth.
1.20: 1.20 And Joktan. Jerome. The later names of these peoples I could not find, but up to the present, because they are far from us, either they are called as at first, or the changed names are unknown; they possessed from the river Cophen the whole region of India which is called Hieria.
1.24: 1.24 Shem, Arphaxad. Rabanus. As in the beginning he placed ten generations from Adam to Noah, so from Shem to Abram, not without the mystery of a sacrament.
1.29: 1.29 The firstborn. Jerome, Questions on Paralipomenon, vol. 3. Twelve sons are born to Ishmael: the firstborn Nebaioth, from whom the whole region from the Euphrates to the Red Sea is called Nabathene: which is a part of Arabia. For their families and towns and villages, and small forts and tribes are celebrated by the name of these; from one of them Kedar in the desert: and Dumah another region, and Thebaram to the south, and Kedemah to the eastern quarter.
1.32: 1.32 Keturah. Rabanus. As if joined, whence the Hebrews suspect that she is Hagar, who, Sarah having died, passed from concubine to wife, lest the old man be accused of lust in new marriages. The same. The sons of Keturah, according to the Hebrew historians, occupied Troconitis, others Traconitis, and Arabia: which is now called Eidormo, as far as the bounds of the Red Sea. Asshurim. Some contend that the Syrians were called from Asshurim, and that the regions of India were occupied by many of the sons of Abraham by Keturah.
1.33: 1.33 Epher. Rabanus. He is said to have led an army against Libya, there to have settled as victor, and his descendants to have named Africa from his name.
1.36: 1.36 Timna. It is asked, since Timna is read in Genesis to be a concubine of Eliphaz of the race of the Horites, who dwelt among the Idumeans in the land of Seir, who bore him Amalek, how she is numbered among the sons, since in what follows this Timna is read as the sister of Lotan son of Seir, who is also Edom? But Seir in Hebrew means hairy, who was rough like a hide. Edom in Hebrew means red or tawny. From the fact that he sold his birthright for red food, he was called Edom. The Hebrews resolve it thus. They say Timna was a concubine of Eliphaz and bore him Amalek, but was brought up by him among the sons as a daughter.
1.40: 1.40 Alian, who is of the race of the Horites. In Genesis it is written Alvah, that is exalted. In Paralipomenon, however, Alian, that is cast out, signifying that the Horites were exalted before Edom took their land, but afterward cast out. Shephi. Jerome. That is, one-footed. In Genesis Shepho, that is, two-footed; both however with the letter shin. He is called two-footed because with the passage of time, by the multitude of his offspring, he had greater efficacy than at first.
1.41: 1.41 Hamran. In Paralipomenon Hamram, that is reddened, filthy or tumultuous. In Genesis Hemdan, that is desirable; but both are names of one man.
1.42: 1.42 Jaakan. Rabanus. Jaakan son of Ezer of the race of the Horites, in Genesis is named Akan, that is troubler. In Paralipomenon Jaakan, that is troubled. For names are changed by varying events, that various mysteries may be signified.
1.43: 1.43 Dinhabah. The city of Bela son of Beor king of Edom, after whom Jobab reigned. There is yet to this day a village Dinhabah, at the eighth mile from Areopolis, for those going to Armon, and another Dinhabah on the mount Peor, at the seventh stone of Jebus. Jerome, concerning the Jesbites.
1.44: 1.44 Jobab son of Zerah, whom they suspect to be Job. But the Hebrews assert that he was born of the stock of Nahor; Philo, however, in the book of Questions on Genesis, relates that he lived in these times and took as wife Dinah, daughter of Jacob: and before the contest of his temptation he says she bore him seven sons and three daughters, who were destroyed in the temptation. But when he was healed the Lord restored to him all things double, and his wife again bore the aforesaid seven sons and three daughters, whose names were the same as those of the former, that is, Eliphaz, Armoe, Diasath, Philasia, Dipharceluth, Thelon, and of the daughters Meru, Lizath, Zeli. Bozrah, etc. Which is Bosor, a city in the desert beyond the Jordan in the tribe of Reuben. Another Bosor is also called, a city of Esau in the mountains of Idumea, of which it is said: His garments tawny from Bosor
1.45: 1.45 Of the Temanites. Teman, a region that took its name from Teman son of Eliphaz. There is to this day a village Teman, five miles distant from the city of Petra, and where a garrison of Roman soldiers was stationed, from which place was Eliphaz king of the Temanites: one of the sons of Ishmael was also called Teman. It must be known that every southern region is called Teman in Hebrew.
1.46: 1.46 Midian, a city so called from the youngest of the sons of Abraham and Keturah. It is beyond Arabia in the desert of the Saracens toward the east of the Red Sea, whence they are called Midianites, and the region Midianite. The daughters of the father-in-law of Moses are also called daughters of Midian; but this is another city of the same name near Armon and Areopolis, whose ruins are still shown.
1.48: 1.48 Rehoboth. A city by the river where the king of Edom was, and to this day there is a garrison in the region of Gabalene, and a large village so called.
1.50: 1.50 Matred's daughters, etc. Two mothers are here counted, to signify a mystery, that a goldsmith begot a steward, and the steward the kindness of the Lord, because from depth of sense is born fruitful speech, which deserves to beget in the hearts of the hearers a pure faith, the grace of God.
1.51: 1.51 Dukes, etc. It is to be noted that he first said kings of Edom, afterward dukes, though they came first: of whom he names some mothers, such as Oholibamah and Timna. Duke Aliah. Alvah is read in Genesis, whose interpretation is elevation; in Paralipomenon Aliah, that is, over her.
2.1: 2.1 Achar who. Jerome, Questions on Paralipomenon, vol. 3. Achar, who is also called Achan in Joshua, that is, a lurking serpent, Achar troubled, etc., down to that is, they were destroyed by the multitude of sins.
2.9: 2.9 Chelubai, that is, my dog, who is also Caleb, that is dog, one of the spies. Hezron and Jephunneh are also the same, hence Caleb is read as son of Hezron and sometimes son of Jephunneh.
2.13: 2.13 And Jesse begot. In the book of Kings Jesse is said to have eight sons, in Paralipomenon no more than seven. But the Hebrews say that Nathan the prophet was the son of Shammah, or Shammua, or Shimea, son of Jesse, whom he brought up and nourished in place of a son, numbered among the sons. Among the sons of Jesse, Nathan was also brought to Samuel, who is also Jonathan, who struck the lion. And it must be known that where he is called prophet, Nathan is written, not Jonathan.
2.17: 2.17 Jether. In Kings, Jethra the Israelite; but the quality of merits makes the diversity of names; for Jethra is interpreted remnant, Jether a small remnant, and Israelite is joined to remnant, Ishmaelite to small remnant.
2.19: 2.19 Ephrath. Jerome. This is Miriam the sister of Moses, mother of Hur, father of Uri, grandfather of Bezalel. Hur is he who with Aaron held up the hands of Moses while Joshua fought.
2.22: 2.22 Jair. He was a judge after Tola and judged Israel twenty-two years, having thirty sons, princes of thirty cities, which were named from him, as is read in the book of Judges.
2.25: 2.25 Were born. Thus far the writer of the history has woven the generation of two sons of Hezron, the two later ones, that is, Ram and Chelubai, of whom he first told; because he wished the royal and priestly dignity to be known in any way. Now he returns to the genealogy of the firstborn, that is Jerahmeel.
2.26: 2.26 Onam. He took his name from Onan son of Judah, but they differ, because the son of Judah is written with Nun, the son of Jerahmeel with Mem.
2.34: 2.34 Sheshan. The Hebrews say he is Elimelech, husband of Naomi, father of Mahlon and Chilion, and therefore the writer in what follows hints that Sheshan had no sons but daughters, because his two sons died without children.
2.43: 2.43 Hebron. The city in which David reigned seven years before he reigned in Jerusalem. It signifies that these places received names from the descendants of Caleb, who received Hebron and its suburbs as his lot.
2.50: 2.50 These were the sons. He recapitulates the generation of Caleb from Ephrath, which he left off before, when he told of Hur begotten of Ephrath, that is, Miriam the sister of Moses.
2.52: 2.52 Kiriath-jearim, which is also Kiriath-baal, that is city of the woods, one of the cities of the Gibeonites at the ninth mile for those going from Aelia to Diospolis in the tribe of Judah.
2.54: 2.54 Bethlehem; the city of David, in the tribe of Judah, in which the Lord was born, at the seventh mile from Aelia toward the southern quarter, beside the road that leads to Hebron, where the tomb of Jesse and David is shown, and about a thousand paces off the tower of Eder, that is tower of the flock, in a certain prophecy signifying beforehand the shepherds aware of the Lord's nativity. Who divided half of the resting places. Jerome, as above, that is, he received the lots of Midian beside the tombs of the patriarchs which are in Kiriath-arba, and his sons were the Ithrites, etc. The Zorites and the Eshtaulites received names of places, which are Zorah and Eshtaol, where Samson was buried. For a resting place is called a tomb. Others understand the half of the resting as half the time in which the children of Israel began to possess the promised land, namely from the time when Moses gave the land of Gilead beyond the Jordan to Reuben and Gad and the half tribe of Manasseh, until the other tribes received their lots. In the middle of this time they say Shobal died, and so saw half the resting places, that is, reached the middle of that time. Mystically, however, Shobal, that is vain antiquity, or a bar for carrying, signifies the Jews, who of old were called the people of God and first received the law of the letter, who carried the books of the law and the prophets, but did not understand the mystery of the incarnation of Christ. Hence they saw half the resting places, that is, the history. But he possesses the fullness of rests who after very good works rejoices in eternal rest. Or he sees half the rest who after the labor of the present life has the rest of the soul. He will then see the perfection of the rests when he enjoys the perfection of rest in both soul and body.
2.55: 2.55 Of the dwellers. The same. The Hebrews relate that Jabez was a most skilled teacher of the law, in whose sight sat the sons of the Kenites, who are also Jobab, kinsmen of Moses. Scribes are therefore said to be singers and resounding ones, because they were assiduously occupied in the speech of the law of God: the history of the kings also tells that they dwelt in tents. Jabez signifies Christ, the true master of the saints singing praises to God. For Jabez is interpreted drying, and Christ dried up in his faithful the flow of carnal desires. The Kenites, that is possession or possessors, are all the elect, of whom it is said: Israel is my inheritance, and whose possession is the Lord. Rechab is interpreted charioteer or ascending. These came from the heat of the father of the house of Rechab, because, inflamed by the grace of the Spirit from the Father of lights, they ascend into the heavens by the four-horse chariot of virtues, of whom it is said: As many as are led by the Spirit of God, these are the sons of God (Rom. 8).
3.1: 3.1 And David. He returns to set forth the offspring of David, which he left before, when, enumerating the offspring of Ram son of Hezron, he came to Jesse and his sons, of whom David was the last. By Ahinoam the Jezreelitess. Rabanus. Jezreel is the city in which Naboth dwelt, whom Jezebel killed. Daniel. The same. Daniel, who in the book of Kings is Chileab, that is, avenging his father, because, according to the Hebrews, disputing with Mephibosheth over questions of the law, he appeared victor and seemed to avenge his father in him, lest a warlike man be mocked in disputation by a weak man.
3.3: 3.3 Of Eglah his wife. Jerome. It is asked why this Eglah alone is called David's wife; but this is Michal, who among many alone is called wife, because he took her first as wife in his youth, who is said to have died in childbirth. Eglah is interpreted heifer, which signifies the Synagogue, which took on the yoke of the law but corrupted it by wantonness, hence, Ephraim a heifer taught to love threshing. Our David took her when he joined her to himself in the testament given. She died in childbirth, because when the Word of God appeared in the flesh and preached the Gospel, when through faith she ought to have borne offspring of good works, scandalized by his passion she brought eternal death upon herself.
3.4: 3.4 In Hebron, where he reigned, etc. What is to be understood by the reign of David in Hebron or in Jerusalem we have touched on in expounding the book of Kings. It is written in what follows: All the time in which David reigned was forty years; he reigned in Hebron seven years, in Jerusalem thirty-three, hence it is asked why forty years and six months are not counted in the sum; the Hebrews say that David fled from his son Absalom for six months, and these were deservedly excluded from the sum of his reign. They also say that for six months in Hebron he labored under bodily illness, and therefore they are not rightly reckoned in the reign. For they say he reigned in Hebron from the time that, the Amalekites having been conquered, he sent from their spoils to the elders of Judah, namely those who were in Hebron and others.
3.9: 3.9 All these were the sons of David, etc. Because all the sons of Christ await the eternal palm, but the sons of concubines are excepted, who among the rest did not deserve to be numbered by name. For Jewish heretics or schismatics cannot have fellowship in this company: the glory of the heavenly kingdom awaits the sons of David only from a noble marriage. For the son of the bondwoman shall not be heir with the son of the free woman (Gen. 21).
3.15: 3.15 And the sons of Josiah. Rabanus. Four sons of Josiah are read here, etc., down to who was likewise carried off to the Chaldeans.
3.17: 3.17 Assir, Shealtiel, Malchiram, Pedaiah, Shenazzar, etc. These names are of one man, as the Hebrews hold; he is Pedaiah father of Zerubbabel and Shimei. Hence in Ezra and in Matthew Zerubbabel is written as son of Shealtiel. And Pedaiah is interpreted redeemed of the Lord, Assir imprisoned, Shealtiel shoot of the Lord; all of which suit holy teachers, by whose office the ecclesiastical people is begotten, who, chastened by various afflictions, redeemed by the grace of the Lord, bring forth shoots of virtues both in themselves and in their subjects.
3.18: 3.18 Shenazzar. He is Sheshbazzar to whom Cyrus counted out the vessels of the house of the Lord, as is said in Ezra. Shenazzar means formed, Sheshbazzar troubled, which suit the keepers of the vessels of God, that is of holy souls, whom Christ, whom Cyrus signified by name and by release, to whom it is said: Ask of me and I will give you the nations for your inheritance (Ps. 2), and who released the captivity of the human race, counted out to be guarded, which are the vessels of the Lord numbered, because the Lord knows who are his (2 Tim. 2).
4.1: 4.1 The sons of Judah. How Perez and Hezron and the three who follow are said to be sons of Judah, when elsewhere we read Perez and Zerah as sons of Judah and Hezron as son of Perez; but the Hebrews assert that, the names being changed, the same sons of Judah whom Scripture names elsewhere by other names are expressed here. For they say Perez, which is interpreted division, has his own proper name here. Hezron is Zerah, but Hezron is interpreted court, Zerah rising. Carmi also is Hur, for Carmi is interpreted my vineyard, Her watching. They say Ur is Onam, but Ur is interpreted left, Onam murmuring, and Shobal is Shelah, the youngest of the sons of Judah whom Shua bore him. Shobal is interpreted ear of grain, or vain antiquity. Shelah sent or his shadow.
4.3: 4.3 Hazzelelponi. Rabanus. They suspect she is the mother of Samson, born of the stock of Judah, whose husband Manoah of the tribe of Dan, who is also read in the book of Judges to be from Zorah.
4.4: 4.4 Gedor and Ezer. The same. These are places possessed by the sons of Hur; but it is strange that here Hur is called father of Bethlehem, when above Salma is called its father, unless perhaps he here calls kinsman father, because Hur was father of Salma who was father of Bethlehem.
4.9: 4.9 And Jabez was. The same. The order seems confused, because having counted the sons of Helah and Naarah, he suddenly introduces the kinship of Aharhel son of Harum, and consequently tells of Jabez; but the Hebrews say that Ashhur by Helah begot Etam, and he Koz. Koz begot Zobebah, and Zobebah Jabez, who was a teacher of scribes. Between Koz and Jabez are inserted the kinships of Aharhel or Aharahel, otherwise Aral, because he is Hobab son of Raguel, that is, Jethro, kinsman of Moses. And because Jabez taught them, they are inserted in his lineage as if begotten by his ancestors. And the mother is the Synagogue from which Christ was born, who bore him in sorrow, because she grieved over his coming on account of unbelief, whence the Jews, envying, said: If we let him alone thus, all will believe in him (John 11).
4.10: 4.10 He called upon. This befits Christ, whom the Father sanctified and sent into the world; of whom it is said: Behold the Lamb of God who takes away the sins of the world, etc. (John 1). God blessed him with the multiplication of sons, whom the most holy Church bears through the water of baptism (1 Cor. 1). He enlarged his borders, because he gave him the inheritance of all the nations, and extended his possession to the ends of the earth. With whom was the hand of the Lord, because the power of the Godhead worked through him powers and miracles. He is also the power and wisdom of God, through whom the Father made all things that are in heaven and on earth, whom the malice of the Jews could not harm, who says of himself: The prince of this world comes, and has nothing in me. Through him also his members are blessed, that is, the Church, to whom it is said through Isaiah: Enlarge the place of your tent, etc. (Isa. 54). With him is the hand of the Lord, because in her works the Son of God, who is the arm and right hand of the Father. And the gates of hell shall not prevail against him, nor shall the devil rule over him, because power has been given him over all the strength of the enemy.
4.11: 4.11 And Chelub the brother. Rabanus. We read above that Caleb is the son of Hezron, whose brothers were Ram and Jerahmeel. The Hebrews therefore say that Ram is here called Chelub, brother of Shuah. Ram is interpreted exalted, Shuah humble, which befits the Jewish people, because it was exalted in the worship of one God and the power of the kingdom; but because it would not receive the Son of God, it was made humble and vile, that the last may become first.
4.12: 4.12 The same. Recah. Some think that Recah is a name of David. For Recah is tender. Hence David says of himself: I am tender and an anointed king (2 Kings 3). He too is said to be like a tender worm of the wood. They are called men of Recah because they are noted here to express the genealogy of David.
4.13: 4.13 And Seraiah begot. Of Seraiah it is said that Joab came forth, who according to the interpretation of the name is called father of the valley of craftsmen, because of his sons were architects who built the house of the Lord. The craftsmen who dwell in the valley can be called teachers of the law, whom knowledge does not puff up, but charity builds up (1 Cor. 8), whom modesty and humility exalt, like Gamaliel and Paul his disciple (Acts 5, 22).
4.17: 4.17 Ezrah. Rabanus, Jerome. The Hebrews say that Ezrah, which is interpreted helper, is Amram the father of Moses and Aaron; Jether, that is help, is Aaron; and Mered, the rebel, is Moses. Epher or Opher, that is dust, was Heldad. And Jalon and Meldath, who were two of the seventy elders whom Moses received from God as help in ruling the people: for they relate that Moses, after receiving the law in the wilderness, persuaded his father to put away his mother, because she was his own aunt, for she was a daughter of Levi, after Amram took another by whom he had Eldad and Medad. And she bore Miriam. The same. They would have Shammai understood as Moses, etc., down to because he governed the people in the wilderness, and by his teaching governs daily.
4.18: 4.18 The daughter of Pharaoh. The same. He calls the daughter of Pharaoh the mother of Moses, who according to the property of the name is also called daughter of the Lord, because she had a good will in nourishing the boy, and Amared, that is, said to have received Moses, because, the idols being forsaken, she was converted to the worship of God.
4.21: 4.21 Er the father. The same. He returns to the offspring of Perez from whom David arose, so that the offspring of Judah from which the royal tribe arose might end in David. For they relate that this was Elimelech, husband of Naomi, in whose time, because of the transgressors of the law, the sun stood still, that having seen the miracle they might be converted to the Lord; because they despised it, famine grew strong, and he who seemed first in the tribe of Judah, driven by want, was expelled from his country with his wife and sons, and died in exile with his sons.
4.22: 4.22 Jokim and Joash. The same. Mahlon and Chilion, who are here called Jokim and Joash (Secure and Burning), were in Moab, because they took Moabite wives, hence in the Hebrew they are called not princes but husbands, as the teachers of that language relate. Who returned into, etc. Naomi and Ruth, who returned to Bethlehem when they heard of the abundance of bread.
4.23: 4.23 The potters dwelling. By potters who labor in plantations and hedges we understand teachers, who form and compose the vessels of the Lord, for to fashion we call to compose, hence the composers of clay we call potters. These plant and cultivate the vineyard of the Lord with doctrine, and fortify it by exhorting and praying. These abide with the king in their works, because, remaining in the faith of Christ, whatever they say, whatever they do, they do to the glory of God.
4.28: 4.28 They dwelt in, etc. The offspring of Ruth, who is said to have dwelt in the very hedges and plantations, when this plantation came to royal dignity and the protection of the people. And they dwelt there. In Genesis six are written, but here Zohar is omitted: because no offspring came from him. But certain names are changed for their own reasons. In Genesis Jemuel, that is mother of God; here Hamuel, that is reading with God. One in Genesis is called Ohad, here however Jarib, that is quarreling, because from him came Zimri, who, fornicating with the Midianite woman, was slain by Phinehas the priest. Jachin in Genesis, that is preparation; here he is named Zerah, that is rising. And the whole kindred not, etc. Because Simeon did not have as much offspring as Judah; hence in Joshua it is said: Simeon received an inheritance through his kindreds in the midst of the sons of Judah. These cities, etc. Because Ziklag and Beersheba, which had been Judah's and were invaded by Simeon, returned from David to the former inheritance of Judah.
4.38: 4.38 These mentioned by name. The stock of Simeon and their acts having been described, it is signified mystically that holy teachers, that is the princes of the Church, providing pastures for the flocks of Christ, set out for Gedor or Gader, which is interpreted his hedge. This is the Church, which is the defense of the faithful: there are the pastures up to the east of the valley, that is, the incarnation of the Word, who emptied himself, taking the form of a servant (Phil. 1). In him pastures are found. For he himself says: If anyone enters through me, he shall go in and go out and find pastures (John 10), namely virtues. In him is the land very wide and quiet, that is, the abundant grace of the Holy Spirit; in which formerly the descendants of Ham had dwelt, signifying that a multitude of nations left the idols and flowed together to the worship of the one God. These then came whom we have described above by name in the days of Hezekiah king of Judah, that is in the coming of Christ. For he is Christ the power of God, whom Hezekiah, namely strength of the Lord, signifies. They struck the tents: he strikes by faith the tents of the impious and the dwellers of the impious when, denying all impiety and worldly desires, he is washed from the filth of sins by the baptism of Christ, afterward striving to live soberly, justly and piously in this world, that it may be fulfilled what is written: And it shall be in the place where it was said before: You are not my people: there they shall be called sons of God (Hos. 1).
4.42: 4.42 Five hundred men. The fathers of the New Testament who went to Mount Seir and struck the remnants of the Amalekites, because, trampling on the pride of this world, they crush the deformity of vices; these are said to be four, because, truly instructed in evangelical doctrine, they fittingly wage spiritual war against demons; the remnants of the Amalekites being struck, they dwelt there, because, demons being expelled, they put virtues in the place of vices, the possession of which makes a man blessed unto this day, which can always be said until the end of the world, because the Church remains until the end of the world, in which daily the ancient enemy is triumphed over.
5.1: 5.1 But since you defiled, etc. Rabanus. The birthright was taken from Reuben because he slept with Bilhah, his father's concubine, and was given to Joseph the younger son, whose offspring is multiplied and exceeds the power of the kingdom among the ten tribes. Mystically, however, it signifies the downfall of the former people, who as firstborn ought to have received the priesthood and kingdom; but because they defiled the couch of their father, that is the body of Christ, in which was the fullness of the Godhead, hanging him on the cross and killing him: the dignity of the firstborn was transferred to the spiritual Joseph, that is Christ and the people of the Church; to whom the Father says: You are a priest forever according to the order of Melchizedek, etc. (Ps. 109).
5.10: 5.10 Against the Hagarites. Jerome in Paralipomenon. It is likely that Hagar was Keturah, since in what follows he says that the Reubenites and Gadites and the half tribe of Manasseh fought with the Hagarites and that Jetur, Naphish and Nodab sons of Ishmael gave Israel help. Nodab is, as it seems, he who in Genesis is called Kedemah, that is of the ancients or going before.
5.26: 5.26 And he stirred up. It is to be noted that in Kings Pul king of the Assyrians is said to have received a thousand talents of silver from Menahem son of Gadi king of Israel (4 Kings 15), to be of help to him and strengthen his kingdom, not that he carried him over to the Assyrians, but that Tiglath-pileser king of Assyria in the days of Pekah king of Israel took Ijon, and Abel-beth-maacah, and Janoah and Kedesh and Hazor and Gilead and Galilee and all the land of Naphtali, and carried them to the Assyrians. Finally it is told that Shalmaneser king of the Assyrians, besieging Hoshea son of Elah king of Israel, took Samaria after three years, and carried Israel to the Assyrians and settled them in Halah and in Habor, by the river Gozan in the cities of the Medes. Hence it is asked: how do we say in Paralipomenon that Pul and Tiglath-pileser kings of the Assyrians carried Reuben and Gad and the half tribe of Manasseh into Halah and Habor and Hara and the river Gozan; when Kings relates that Shalmaneser did this, who carried Israel to the Assyrians and settled them in the aforesaid places? But the earlier kings of the Assyrians are said to have done this, because they began with the nation of the Assyrians what the same nation completed in their descendants. Hara, which Paralipomenon mentions, Kings omits. The Hebrews think it is Rages, a city of the Medes.
6.6: 6.6 The sons of Levi, Gershom, etc. Johanan. Other sons of Levi who were likewise priests in the house of the Lord having been passed over, Johanan is specially praised, because he manfully withstood king Uzziah who wished to sacrifice by himself: and by constancy of mind and zeal for the law he fulfilled the office of priest.
6.15: 6.15 And Jehozadak. Jerome, Hebrew Questions on Paralipomenon. They say Jehozadak is Ezra the priest, etc., down to that Ezra is a priest, a just and glorious man.
6.28: 6.28 Abijah. He, as the Hebrews relate, being appointed a judge, took gifts, which Joel, who is also Vashni, his elder son, knowing, did not correct: therefore both are said to have sinned according to the Hebrew. Hence: When Samuel had grown old, he set his sons as judges over Israel, and the rest.
6.31: 6.31 These are they whom he appointed, anticipating concerning the offices, of the singers of David who sang the praises of the Lord with musical instruments; when he narrated their genealogy, he gave a foretaste; in its own order he will show how they had done it.
6.44: 6.44 Ethan son of. Ethan one of the singers of the tribe, who before David sounded the praise of God on cymbals. And it must be noted that, as there were three sons of Levi, Kohath, Gershom and Merari, so three singers: Heman from Kohath, Asaph from Gershom; Ethan from Merari. Mystically they signify holy teachers, who, imbued with faith in the holy Trinity, according to the dispensation of the true David announce the preaching of the Gospel to the whole world.
6.48: 6.48 The Levites who. Because every ecclesiastical order according to the tradition of the apostles, and those who hold primacy, perform the whole ministry in the Church of God; hence: That you may know how you ought to behave in the house of God, which is the Church of the living God, etc. (1 Tim. 3).
6.49: 6.49 Aaron. He signifies Christ, his sons the people of the Church, to whom it is said: You are a chosen race, a royal priesthood, etc. (1 Pet. 2), whom the high priest taught to offer upon the altar of faith the holocaust of good works and the incense of prayer; and to pray for Israel, that is for the state of the Church, according to the precepts of the law given through Moses. He repeats the genealogy of Aaron down to Ahimaaz, which seems done in his praise, because he was most faithful to David in all things.
7.8: 7.8 All these, the sons of Becher. Wherever in the law it is written: All these are sons of this or that man, it is either for excellence of merits, or for deterioration of merits, so that they are called sons of him whose imitators they were.
7.14: 7.14 And his concubine. She is said to have been the daughter of the son of Balaam, who, led into Egypt for sale by her father under the compulsion of famine, was mercifully taken in marriage by Manasseh, who was in charge of the granaries of food given to his father.
7.15: 7.15 Huppim, etc. These two names are said to be of the former son of Machir, but according to the others they are Zelophehad and their sister Maacah, whom Hezron took as wife when he was sixty years old, who bore him a son Segub, as was said above.
7.18: 7.18 And his sister Hammolecheth (the Queen). The sister of Ulam son of Perez, son of Machir, as was said before; some relate that she was the mother of Joshua son of Nun, who is called a comely man for his remarkable virtue and leadership. Others say Deborah the wife of Lappidoth, a prophetess.
7.20: 7.20 And the sons of Ephraim. The Hebrews tell a tale that the sons of Ephraim, a multitude having gathered, while their father lived, tried to return to the promised land, and were killed in Gath of the Philistines, hence the other tribes are led through the desert, lest they see the bones of their brothers, and it is said in the psalm: The sons of Ephraim turned back in the day of battle (Ps. 77).
8.6: 8.6 Who were carried away to Manahath. When for the crime against the Levite's wife they fell by the sword and only six hundred remained.
8.7: 8.7 Naaman and Ahijah: they were princes, but they submitted to Gera. Hence it is said singularly: He carried them away, from whom came the offspring of Gera who was the father of Shimei.
9.2: 9.2 The Nethinim. Jerome, Questions on Paralipomenon, vol. 3. Gift, or serving in humility. These are the Gibeonites whom Joshua granted life, and assigned to the service of the temple, to bring water and wood (Josh. 9).
9.11: 9.11 Of Hilkiah the sons of Meshullam, etc. He was the high priest who found Deuteronomy in the temple of the Lord in the time of Josiah, and is said to have been the father of the prophet Jeremiah.
9.16: 9.16 Jeduthun. Jerome. Namely the singer of David. For the singers of the sons of Levi in turn kept watch in the king's gate toward the east, and by turns came to sing psalms with David, because before the temple was built the ark of the covenant was in the palace, and there the temple keepers served.
9.19: 9.19 And Shallum son of Kore. The former Kora is written with Aleph, and sounds Cora, the second with He, and sounds Core. Cora is interpreted crying, Core bald. This is he who in Numbers raised a sedition against Moses (Num. 16). Keepers of the thresholds. Jerome. Because they guarded the outer door of the tabernacle. Their fathers, written below, who have titles in the Psalter, guarded the inner door and were singers.
9.20: 9.20 And Phinehas. Grandson of Aaron, who was still living, as the Hebrews relate, and ordered the courses of the ministers. There are twenty-four courses which David ordained for the ministry of the tabernacle. Hence in the Gospel: Zacharias of the course of Abijah (Luke 1).
9.26: 9.26 To these four Levites, etc. Rabanus. Who these four Levites were to whom the whole number of porters was entrusted is shown when it says: Of Hosah, that is of the sons of Merari, Shimri the chief, etc., as in chapter 26. The four chiefs of the porters are the holy teachers who, keeping the door of faith by the four Gospels, open it to believers and close it to blasphemers, to whom with Peter the keys were committed (Matt. 16). They guard the doors through the four winds, because through the four quarters of the world they call the nations to the faith, and watchfully keep the Church.
9.28: 9.28 Of their race were also those over the vessels, the minister. The same. Mystically, they are ordained from the company of holy preachers, who have a vigilant guard over the vessels of the Lord, that is the souls of the faithful in whom the will of God is daily ministered. Under their guard are fine flour, wine and oil, with which the sacraments of the body and blood of the Lord are made, and the grace of the Holy Spirit is conferred by spiritual anointing. They themselves compose the incense of prayers and the spices of virtues in the Church, and render wine acceptable in the sight of the Lord.
9.31: 9.31 Mattithiah the Levite, firstborn of Shallum the Korahite, was over the things fried in the pan. Because Christ is the author of the heavenly sacraments, where daily bread and wine are offered in memory of his passion, and the head of all who crucify their flesh after his example and deliver themselves to the passion for his name.
9.32: 9.32 The showbread. Two and two were baked separately before the sabbath, according to Josephus, and on the sabbath morning were placed on the table, of which we spoke more fully in Leviticus.
9.34: 9.34 The heads of the Levites by their families. It is fitting that the more one is set over others, the more devout he be in the divine offices. He rightly keeps the primacy of the ministry who strives to remain in Jerusalem, that is in the vision of peace, that he may flee the tumult of the world and the pleasures of the flesh and have quiet of mind in the contemplation of God, saying with the Psalmist: I rejoiced in the things that were said to me.
9.35: 9.35 Jehiel, who in Kings is Abiel, father of Kish the father of Saul, and is interpreted my father God. Jehiel eloquent of God, perhaps from the difference of merits. And it must be noted that among the sons of Jehiel, Kish and Ner are called brothers and are, and in Kings it is so; in what follows, however, it is said that Ner begot Kish, not that he begot but that he brought him up.
9.39: 9.39 Abinadab. He, as in Kings, is told to have been killed with his father, is called Abinadab and is interpreted Abinadab my father a vow, Abinadab my people a vow. Eshbaal. Fire husband, he is Ishbosheth, that is man of confusion.
9.40: 9.40 Merib-baal. Contending against the husband, he is Mephibosheth, which is interpreted from the mouth shame.
10.1: 10.1 The Philistines, etc. Rabanus. Many things being omitted which the history in the book of Samuel tells of Samuel and Saul, he recalls the fall of Saul and his family. Mystically hinting that it is not necessary to describe the life of him whose impious conduct deserved to receive a swift end, and figuratively he shows the end of the kingdom of the Jews and of the old priesthood. He passed over to David, whose deeds and the dispensation of the kingdom he weaves, who bears the type of the true David possessing the kingdom of heaven and earth. When he draws near the Philistines in their manner fight against Israel, and conquer, because, as grace approaches, the Gentiles, as before, assailed the chastity of the Israelite faith; now by showing evil works, now the worship of idolatry, as Balaam taught Balak to put a scandal before the children of Israel, to eat and to fornicate. And the men fled. Those who seemed strong in contemplation of God, while incautiously they follow the works and doctrine of the Gentiles; secular knowledge also not a little helped the destruction of heretics. Hence someone said: The philosophers are the patriarchs of heretics; they stained the purity of the Church with perverse doctrine.
10.2: 10.2 And when they had drawn near. The Gentiles rushed in from every side upon the kingdom of Judah and its sons, and corrupted the priests, scribes and Pharisees, the sons, namely, and seducers of that kingdom; and heretics also forbade that they preach or cultivate the grace of the Holy Spirit simply. Abinadab. Lest we should praise with worthy confession the Father who adopted us to himself by spiritual gift, which the killing signifies, Abinadab, that is of my willing father. Malchishua. Lest in the kingdom of Christ we believe that salvation is to come. For Malchishua is interpreted my king salvation. The philosopher who seduced Arius, as it were, killed Malchishua: he who seduced Macedonius, Jonathan; he who seduced Mani, Abinadab. Because the master of corruption taught that one to deny the omnipotence of Christ the true king, another to disparage the gifts of the Holy Spirit, that one to blaspheme the goodness of the supreme Father.
10.4: 10.4 And Saul said to, etc. The Hebrews say this was Doeg the Edomite, who, seeing that Saul was dead, fearing David, killed himself. The young man, because he brought the diadem and bracelet of Saul to David, was the son of Doeg, and Doeg himself was the servant with whom Saul sought the asses of his father. To the armor-bearer. Bede on chapter 28 of book 1 of Kings. Teachers of the law. For as the arms and arrows of the Philistines, etc., down to that they might not be defiled, but might eat the Passover. But the armor-bearer was unwilling. It is not to be doubted that among the reprobate teachers of the law there were some who were unwilling to pervert the sharpness of the word to kill the hearers, and yet the hearers themselves, who had rightly received what was said by their masters, by despising or blaspheming, turned it to their own destruction: whose death having been seen, that is the obstinacy of sinning, the very ministers of the word, deteriorated through the times, made the testimonies of the law, which they had feared to interpret ill, an occasion of ruin for themselves. Heretics also, bloodied by the darts of their sins, when they draw divine words into argument for their error, turn their arms against their own breast, about to die. Any Catholic too, when he pollutes with the contagion of pride, vainglory, avarice or any vice the art which he learned for common usefulness, pierces himself with his own sword, because he rushes upon himself with that by which he ought to have been defended from the enemy.
10.5: 10.5 And when his armor-bearer saw this. The unlearned, seeing the remedies of true humility and the washing of baptism, not knowing that in Judea their masters were conquered in spiritual contest, and a not small crowd near to their hearing, with the adversary persecuting, driven from the ancient seat of constancy, troubled by the downfall of their elders, lost the works of virtue and the bulwarks of spiritual knowledge which they had had. And the sins of the Gentiles came, and corrupted by perverse dwelling all the pursuits of virtue of the unbelieving Jews. Unclean spirits came, and occupied the hearts which constancy of faith had deserted. The Gentiles came, and by believing made their own the once best pursuits of the Jews. Hence: The kingdom of God will be taken from you, and given to a nation yielding its fruits (Matt. 21).
10.10: 10.10 And the head. Rabanus on Paralipomenon. The Philistines fastened the head of Saul in the temple of Dagon, etc., down to for Bethshan is another in Judges and Joshua, which is interpreted house of security.
10.11: 10.11 When the men of Jabesh heard this. The same, ibid. The men, namely, of the Church, etc., down to this is the city which Saul at the first beginnings of his reign delivered from the siege of the enemies.
10.12: 10.12 The oak at Jabesh, and they fasted seven days, etc. That they may come to rest. For after the six ages of this world in which we labor in the flesh, follows the seventh of the rest of souls. Mystically, over the blindness of the Jews carnally observing the sabbath, their fellow tribesmen, that is the faithful, continually grieve, and as it were fast seven days. But the mystery of the eighth day, the resurrection, being grasped, both will rejoice in perpetual festivity. Morally, however, holy men detest the death of the impious, and consign their examples to the burial of oblivion. They fast seven days, that is they spend in continence all the time of this life, which rolls on by the sevenfold number of days, and abstain from all evil lest they die likewise.
11.3: 11.3 The elders. Rabanus. The prophets and apostles with equal devotion run together to Christ, hence: The princes of the people are gathered together with the God of Abraham (Ps. 2).
11.5: 11.5 And they said. Setting the blind and lame and lepers upon the walls to the contempt of the king, and saying that the blind and lame kept him out. Mystically, David casting the Jebusite out of Jerusalem signifies Christ expelling demons from the hearts of the faithful, and establishing his dwelling there. For Jebusite is interpreted trodden down, Jerusalem vision of peace. Hence he also says to his disciples: Behold, I have given you power to tread upon serpents, etc. (Luke 10). Rightly, then, it is written in Kings that, the blind and lame who hated the soul having been cast out, David took the stronghold of Zion and called it his city, because when Christ expels the malignant spirits and the crowd of vices from the soul, illuminating it with wisdom, it is deservedly called the stronghold of Zion, that is of watching and vision of peace, of which it is rightly said in Psalm 75: In Judea God is known, in Israel his name is great. And his place is made in peace.
11.8: 11.8 And Joab built up the rest of the city. For by the industry of the soldier he fortified the city. Josephus however says that David fortified the upper city, and by joining the citadel to it made one body and surrounded everything with a wall. He set Jacob over the work of the walls, expelled the Jebusites and called it Jerusalem. For Jero in Hebrew is fortification. Christ also first preached the Gospel in Judea, and strengthened the Church with the fortification of his faith. Joab, who built the rest of the city, signifies the apostles and apostolic men who after the Lord's ascension converted very many of the nations; hence: We are God's helpers, God's field.
11.11: 11.11 Jashobeam. Jerome. Josephus names him Eusebius, and they say he was the son of Ahimaaz, who, frequently rushing into the enemy line, did not cease until he had killed eight hundred. Others understand him to be David, because Jashobeam is interpreted sitting among the people. Hachmonite means very wise, hence in Kings it is written: Sitting in the seat, the wisest (2 Kings 23). But there he is compared to a worm of the wood, because wisdom was diminished in him on account of the sin which he had committed against Uriah. Hence there he is said to have killed eight hundred in one onset, here however three hundred, for reputation was lessened on account of sin.
11.12: 11.12 The Ahohite. Ahohi, as the Hebrews relate, was brother of Jesse the father of David, whose son was Eleazar, who was the most powerful among the three, whom Josephus says to be Eusebius son of Ahimaaz, and Eleazar son of Addi, and Shemaiah son of Eli. Gregory, Homily 34 on the Gospels. We must think with the utmost care, etc., down to rigid against himself he abstained even from lawful things.
11.21: 11.21 But up to the first three. Here it appears that Abishai was chief among the following three. But he did not reach the first three, Jashobeam, Eleazar and Shammah. Mystically it is signified that none of the saints, though eminent in virtues, comes to equality with the power of the Father and the Son and the Holy Spirit. For who in the clouds can be compared to the Lord? etc. (Ps. 88).
11.22: 11.22 Ariel of Moab, that is lions, as it is said in Kings, namely the strongest men in the kingdom of Moab, like lions. He killed a lion. The Hebrew thinks this lion was Joab, who was slain in the house of the Lord holding the horns of the altar. For the altar is called a cistern, because as the water of a cistern cleanses, so the sanctuary of God expiates the sins of men. Rabanus. Whom the book of Kings, etc., down to and wrested the spear which he did not hold rightly. In time of snow. By which can be signified the grace of Christ, which shone upon the world, and the cold of charity by which men grow cold. Benaiah, who is interpreted builder the Lord, signifies Christ, of whom it is said: The Lord building up Jerusalem, etc. (Ps. 146). He accomplished many works, who says: My Father works until now, and I work (John 5). He is of Kabzeel, that is, of the congregation of the Lord, because to him belongs the whole company of the saints, who descending from heaven and made man, by his death killing the lion, that is the devil who possessed the world numb with the cold of his unbelief, plunged him into hell. He overcame by the rod of the cross the Egyptian, that is Antichrist, blackest with sins, that is abusing the five senses of the body for crimes, and condemned the guilty one by his own wickedness to perpetual punishment. In the days of snow, because by death he expiated sin. Hence: You will wash me and I shall be made whiter than snow (Ps. 50).
11.24: 11.24 Among the three. Abishai and Sibbechai and Jonathan, to whom he was equal in strength, who was over the thirty, as the Hebrew affirms.
12.12: 12.12 These also came. Thus far he has enumerated the strong men of David who helped him to reign over Israel. Who were the strongest, etc. According to the letter it signifies that they were agile and vigorous in every kind of fighting. Mystically, however, it describes the soldiers of Christ as not sluggish but zealous in prosperity and in adversity, on the right and on the left.
